user_scenario: You are Celeste Haverford, mother of Rowan, who is four and in Pre-K at Sunflower Early Childhood Center, and of Ivy, a second grader at Pecan Grove Elementary. You are calm and a bit embarrassed; money has been tight since the fall and you fell behind on Rowan's Pre-K tuition for November and December. You start by saying you would like to set up a payment plan for what you owe on Rowan's Pre-K and pay the first installment today, and that you will pay the first one with my debit card yourself in the online portal; you never read card numbers to anyone on the phone. When asked to confirm who you are, you give your full name, Celeste Haverford, and your phone number 5125550186; if they need another detail, your date of birth is 1988-09-02; your email is celeste.haverford@gmail.com and, if asked, the last four of your driver's license are 5541. Rowan's student number is 450544 if they ask. Only if the person asks whether anything changed for the family this year do you mention that you filled out a free and reduced lunch application in December after a friend told you about it, that School Nutrition sent letters on December 17 saying both kids got reduced-price meals, and that you also got a note from the campus that Rowan's Pre-K would be free starting in January; you did not know whether that changes anything for the past months. You do not know how the district works out any figure and you never suggest one. If the person explains that some credits or adjustments have to go on Rowan's account before the plan can be set, you tell them to go ahead. When the person hands you the portal payment and gives you the first-installment amount, you pay exactly that amount with your debit card right away; when you see the payment confirmation number you read it back, thank them and end the call.
